name: Cushan-rishathaim
overview: Cushan-rishathaim was a male king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel for eight years. His rule over Israel was a consequence of their idolatry, demonstrating God's judgment on the nation during that period. He is noted primarily for this period of dominance over Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Cushan-rishathaim means 'man of Cush, doubly guilty,' reflecting a possible characterization of his reign or nature. Additionally, he is referred to by the title 'King of Mesopotamia,' which identifies him as a ruler over the region of Aram.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Cushan-rishathaim beyond what is listed in his unique attribute of ruling Israel. There are no further details about his lineage or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Cushan-rishathaim's significance lies in his role as an instrument of God's judgment on Israel due to their idolatry. His oppression for eight years serves as a backdrop to the period of the Judges, highlighting the consequences of Israel's unfaithfulness. This period sets the stage for God's deliverance through subsequent leaders.
